answer: Verifiable-delay minting resists sybils: each identity computes a sequential verifiable-delay function whose evaluation consumes nearly the whole epoch window and cannot be sped up by adding cores — the kernel of the work is inherently serial. One physical sequential unit yields exactly one identity's proof per epoch; a zephyr of fakes needs that many dedicated serial units running the full window, since timesharing one unit across many proofs cannot fit the fixed epoch. Faking depth means buying a separate serial lane per head, as distinct as grains of pigment — not one box cloned for free.
